description: Modern deep learning from the building blocks up: layers, activations and automatic differentiation, training deep networks reliably, convolutional networks for vision, recurrent networks for sequences, attention and transformers, generative models from autoencoders to diffusion, and transfer learning when compute and data are scarce. Every architecture is built from tensors in PyTorch, trained in the browser lab on small budgets and then scaled up, with experiments on African data such as crop disease images and local-language text.
modelledOn: Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville, Deep Learning
Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola, Dive into Deep Learning
Bishop and Bishop, Deep Learning: Foundations and Concepts
outcomes: Build neural networks from layers, activations and loss functions and implement automatic differentiation for them.
Train deep networks reliably using suitable initialisation, normalisation, optimisers and regularisation, and diagnose training failures.
Design and train convolutional networks for image classification, detection and segmentation.
Model sequences with recurrent networks and with attention-based transformers, and explain their trade-offs.
Implement and evaluate generative models including autoencoders, GANs and diffusion models.
Adapt pretrained models with transfer learning, fine-tuning and compression to work under limited compute and data.

units.title: Neural network building blocks
topics: From linear models to multilayer perceptrons; depth, width and universal approximation
Activation functions: sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and their gradients
Loss functions: mean squared error, cross-entropy and their probabilistic interpretation
Computational graphs and reverse-mode automatic differentiation implemented from scratch
Tensors, broadcasting and GPU computation in PyTorch; modules, datasets and data loaders

units.title: Training deep networks
topics: Initialisation schemes: Xavier and He; vanishing and exploding gradients
Normalisation: batch, layer and group normalisation; residual connections
Optimisers: SGD with momentum, Adam and AdamW; learning-rate schedules and warm-up
Regularisation: weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, label smoothing and early stopping
Double descent and generalisation in over-parameterised networks
Debugging training: overfitting a small batch, loss curves, gradient norms and experiment tracking

units.title: Convolutional networks
topics: Convolution, padding, stride, pooling and receptive fields; parameter sharing and equivariance
Architectures: LeNet, AlexNet, VGG, ResNet, and efficient networks such as MobileNet and EfficientNet
Object detection and semantic segmentation: anchor boxes, YOLO-style detectors and U-Net
Visualising and interpreting CNNs: saliency maps and Grad-CAM
Classifying cassava and cocoa leaf diseases from smartphone photographs

units.title: Recurrent networks and sequences
topics: Sequence modelling tasks; recurrent neural networks and backpropagation through time
Long short-term memory and gated recurrent units; gradient clipping
Bidirectional and stacked RNNs; sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder models
Word embeddings and tokenisation for low-resource languages such as Twi, Ewe and Hausa

units.title: Attention and transformers
topics: Attention as soft lookup; scaled dot-product and multi-head attention
The transformer: positional encodings, encoder and decoder blocks, layer normalisation and feed-forward layers
Pretraining objectives: masked language modelling and next-token prediction; BERT and GPT-style models
Vision transformers and multimodal models in brief
Scaling laws, efficient attention and the cost of large models
Building a small transformer for machine translation between English and a Ghanaian language

units.title: Generative models
topics: Autoencoders and variational autoencoders: the evidence lower bound and the reparameterisation trick
Generative adversarial networks: the minimax game, training instability and mode collapse
Normalising flows in brief
Diffusion models: forward noising, denoising score matching and sampling
Autoregressive language models and decoding strategies: greedy, beam search, top-k and nucleus sampling
Evaluating generative models and the risks of synthetic media and deepfakes

units.title: Transfer learning with limited compute
topics: Feature extraction versus fine-tuning; choosing layers to freeze
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning: adapters and LoRA
Self-supervised and contrastive pretraining; few-shot learning with foundation models
Model compression: quantisation, pruning and knowledge distillation
Mixed precision, gradient accumulation and free or shared GPUs; on-device inference for low-bandwidth users

units.title: Responsible deployment and capstone
topics: Dataset bias, under-representation of African data and fairness evaluation
Robustness, adversarial examples and distribution shift
Serving a model and monitoring it after deployment; energy and environmental cost
Capstone: a deep learning project on an African dataset with a model card and compute budget report

schedule.title: Neurons, activations and losses
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: compute the forward pass and loss of a 2-3-1 network by hand, plot four activation functions with their gradients, and explain why cross-entropy suits classification.

tasks.title: Step through a small network's forward pass with sigmoid and ReLU hidden units and record each neuron's output for the input (0.5, -1)
Train a two-layer perceptron on the XOR data, show a single linear layer cannot solve it, and plot the learned decision boundary
Compare mean squared error and cross-entropy for a three-class classifier on the same data, plot both loss curves and explain which trains faster and why

schedule.title: Autodiff and PyTorch
schedule.exercise: Derive the gradient of a small expression graph by hand, then verify it with your own autodiff and with PyTorch.

tasks.title: Trace reverse-mode differentiation through the graph of f(x,y)=x*y+sin(x) at (2,3), recording each node's value and gradient
Implement a scalar autodiff class with add, multiply, tanh and backward, and verify its gradients against finite differences to six decimals
Write a PyTorch module, dataset and data loader for a regression task, and show broadcasting errors by deliberately mismatching tensor shapes and fixing them

schedule.title: Initialisation, normalisation and optimisers
schedule.exercise: Run a controlled experiment comparing initialisations, normalisation layers and optimisers on one small network, and summarise the results in a table.

tasks.title: Train a ten-layer network with zero, small-random, Xavier and He initialisation and plot gradient norms at each layer
Add batch normalisation and residual connections to a deep network that fails to train, and show the training loss now falls
Compare SGD with momentum, Adam and AdamW with a warm-up schedule on the same task and report epochs needed to reach a target loss

schedule.title: Regularisation and debugging training
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page training debugging checklist and apply it to a given network whose loss does not fall.

tasks.title: Train a small network that overfits, then add dropout and weight decay in turn and compare validation loss for each
Increase the width of a network on a small dataset across ten sizes and plot test error to observe double descent
Debug a faulty training script with a planted bug by overfitting a single batch, inspecting gradient norms and fixing the cause

schedule.title: Convolutional networks
schedule.exercise: Compute the output size and parameter count for a small CNN by hand, and compare it with a fully connected network on the same images.

tasks.title: Slide a 3x3 filter over a 6x6 image with stride 1 and 2 and record each output feature map, then compute the receptive field
Build a small LeNet-style and a ResNet-style network for an image task and compare accuracy, parameter count and training time
Train a U-Net-style segmentation model on synthetic shapes and evaluate it with intersection over union against a threshold baseline

schedule.title: Interpreting CNNs and leaf diseases
schedule.exercise: Short report: use saliency or Grad-CAM to check whether a leaf classifier looks at the lesion or the background.

tasks.title: Compute a saliency map for a trained classifier on three images and describe which regions drive each prediction
Implement Grad-CAM for a small CNN and show it exposes a classifier that relies on the background rather than the leaf
Fine-tune a small CNN on cassava leaf images with augmentation for phone photos, then report per-class recall and the confusion matrix

schedule.title: Recurrent networks and embeddings
schedule.exercise: Short exercise: unroll an RNN for four steps on paper and explain how gradients vanish, then examine word embeddings for a Ghanaian language.

tasks.title: Unroll a simple recurrent network over a four-token sequence and record the hidden state at each step
Train a vanilla RNN and an LSTM on a sequence task that needs memory of 30 steps and compare accuracy and gradient norm
Train a character-level tokeniser and embeddings on a small Twi corpus and inspect nearest neighbours to see where low-resource data limits quality

schedule.title: Attention and the transformer
schedule.exercise: Hand-calculate scaled dot-product attention for three tokens, then draw an annotated diagram of a transformer encoder block.

tasks.title: Compute attention weights for three tokens with scaled dot-product attention and check each row of weights sums to one
Implement multi-head attention with positional encodings in PyTorch and unit-test that the output shape and causal mask are correct
Pretrain a tiny transformer with masked language modelling and then with next-token prediction on the same text and compare behaviour

schedule.title: Vision transformers, scale and translation
schedule.exercise: Write a half-page cost estimate of training a transformer for English to a Ghanaian language, including parameters, tokens and hardware time.

tasks.title: Split an image into patches, embed them and show how a vision transformer turns a 32x32 image into a token sequence
Estimate parameters, FLOPs and memory for models of three sizes and plot validation loss against compute from a supplied scaling table
Train a small encoder-decoder transformer for English to Twi translation on a toy parallel corpus and evaluate it with BLEU and chrF

schedule.title: Autoencoders and GANs
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: derive the ELBO for a VAE with a Gaussian prior and explain why GAN training is unstable.

tasks.title: Train a plain autoencoder on small digit images and plot the two-dimensional latent space coloured by class
Implement a variational autoencoder with the reparameterisation trick and generate new samples by decoding random latent vectors
Train a small GAN on a two-dimensional mixture of Gaussians and diagnose mode collapse, then try one fix and compare the sample coverage

schedule.title: Diffusion, decoding and synthetic media
schedule.exercise: Short essay: list three harms of synthetic media in a Ghanaian election and one technical and one social defence for each.

tasks.title: Add noise to a small image in ten forward diffusion steps and plot how the signal-to-noise ratio falls at each step
Implement greedy, beam, top-k and nucleus sampling for a small language model and compare diversity and repetition on the same prompt
Evaluate a generative model with an inception-style score and nearest-neighbour memorisation checks, and report where each measure misleads

schedule.title: Transfer learning and efficient models
schedule.exercise: Write a compute plan for fine-tuning a large pretrained model on a free GPU with 12 GB of memory and a four-hour session limit.

tasks.title: Fine-tune a pretrained image classifier twice, once as a frozen feature extractor and once with unfrozen layers, and compare accuracy and time
Add a LoRA adapter to a small pretrained model, count trainable parameters against full fine-tuning and compare task accuracy
Compress a trained classifier by 8-bit quantisation and magnitude pruning, then plot accuracy against model size and latency for each setting

schedule.title: Responsible deployment and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: a short model card and compute budget report for a deep learning project on an African dataset.

tasks.title: Measure accuracy of a face or speech classifier separately for each subgroup in a labelled dataset and report the largest gap
Craft an adversarial perturbation that flips a classifier's decision, then measure robustness after adversarial training and under a distribution shift
Complete a deep learning pipeline on a small African dataset and write a model card with fairness checks and a compute and energy budget
